title: How John Rush runs 24 AI products to $3M ARR: validate with Google, waitlists, and pre-sales
summary: John Rush explains how he builds small AI agents and tools as a solo bootstrapper. He covers finding ideas via Google autocomplete and keyword research, validating with waitlists, outreach and discounted pre-bookings, and his five growth channels: social, SEO, affiliates, distribution everywhere, and free tools.

principles.text: Build products that scratch your own itch; run them internally for a year or more before launching publicly.
principles.quote: Well, they all start as my internal agent and I run them for a long while so that I'm happy with them myself and also it's easier to run a project if you're the only customer

principles.text: Mine Google autocomplete and keyword tools for demand in small niches VCs ignore; they are good for million-dollar solo businesses.
principles.quote: it's not a billion dollar idea right but if you're regular person and you want to build a million dollar business that's on of the market right

principles.text: Try to kill your idea during validation; test with a simple waitlist, outreach, then discounted pre-bookings.
principles.quote: if you ask for a payment and you don't get at least 10% of your weight list to, you know, execute it, it means that it won't be easier after, right?

principles.text: Use landing page builders (Framer, Webflow, Unicorn) for landing pages, not vibe coding tools made for apps.
principles.quote: you have landing pages and you have your web app and for landing pages use landing page builder

principles.text: Start SEO on day one as both a traffic channel and a validation signal, since it compounds.
principles.quote: SEO traffic is a new source of validation because you know one thing that you have to also validate with a product is not just if people want it but also if you're able to drive traffic there

principles.text: Offer very generous affiliate commissions (up to 50%) and place your product everywhere, including for LLM training data.
principles.quote: You should be crazy generous. Like go 50%. Like if you don't have costs on your product, go for 50%.
